note: Natural / wild mountain onsens. Entries without lat/lon get their position from OpenStreetMap by name when the places Action runs (tools/build_places.py). Most are snowbound and closed in winter.

onsens.ja: 蓮華温泉 野天風呂
onsens.season: Lodge and pools open about mid-July to late October.
onsens.access: The road in is closed outside summer, so the rest of the year it's a long tour in.
onsens.note: Four rock pools on the slope above the lodge: Ogon-yu, Senki-no-yu, Yakushi-yu and Sangokuichi-no-yu. No changing rooms. About ¥500 for the outdoor pools only.

onsens.season: Early July to late September only.
onsens.access: 4 to 5 hours' hike up from Sarukura.
onsens.note: Open-air pools at about 2,100 m beside the hut. The hut is taken down every autumn because the site sits in an avalanche path all winter.

onsens.season: About April to November. Closed in winter.
onsens.access: Short walk from the top of Tsubame Onsen village.
onsens.note: Free, sunrise to sunset, separate men's and women's pools. Closed Mondays and Friday mornings for cleaning. Bring gumboots during the snowmelt.

onsens.season: About July to November, once the bridge is in. Closed in winter.
onsens.access: About 15 minutes' walk up the gorge from the Myoko-san / Tsubame Onsen trailhead.
onsens.note: Free, mixed, beside the river. Sunrise to sunset.

onsens.access: About 2 hours from the top of the Asahidake ropeway via Susoaidaira.
onsens.note: A true wild bath: a dug pool with no buildings. The source is too hot, so people dig channels to mix in snowmelt. Brown bear country, so carry a bear bell.

onsens.season: Closed November to April. Usually reopens just before Golden Week.
onsens.access: About 2 hours' hike from the end of the Akayu forest road beyond Naeba.
onsens.note: Three river-side outdoor pools at a lamp-lit hut. You can dig your own pool on the riverbank upstream. No phone signal in the valley.
